what_happened: The record's own absorbing duplicate (completed/archived task 373, null_resolution_entries_unreachable_by_conclusion_stage) was found live in this repository's specs/archive/ tree, confirming the dispatch's DISPOSITION PENDING note was correct: the resolution-field half of the defect is fixed, verified byte-identical between agent-system/extensions/core/context/{contracts/conclusion-stage.md,formats/issue-log.md} and the deployed .claude/ mirror, with implicit_open_count present in both the contract and the live orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate output.

The dispatch's DISPOSITION PENDING block treated the 'where does a transplant go when the absorbing record is already closed' question as unresolved, pointing at a foreign repository's record 481 that does not resolve here. A repository-local governing document, agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/cross-repo-task-migration.md's 'Duplicates: transplant before abandoning' section, already states the general rule directly: if amending the absorbing record is not possible, do not abandon the duplicate -- report it and leave it open. No foreign record needs to resolve; this repository's own migration-pattern document already answers the fail-safe case task 562 is in.

Independent reproduction of transplant item (i) did not require cross-repo access to a foreign fixture: a live, currently-active task in this repository (436_orient_command_with_scout_agent_retire_review) already carries 9 null-resolution, null-suggested_channel, kind:issue entries spanning minor and costly severity. Running orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh --aggregate (read-only) against it reproduced the post-fix behavior exactly: all 9 reached classification as 7 proposals (one class grouping 3 entries), implicit_open_count=9, 3 kind:win entries correctly exempted, and every proposal's suggested_channel_hints was an empty array -- corroborating both the reproduction-at-higher-severity requirement and the proposal-volume datum from a second, independent run.

The dispatch description's central 'DECIDE AND LAND ONE OF THREE' framing is superseded: option (b) composed with the surfacing half of option (c) is already landed and verified byte-identical between the core source store and the deployed mirror. The originally-cited reproduction fixture (11 entries, proposals 0/wins 4/unknown_classes 6) is a path from the repository this record migrated from and does not resolve here, so it could not be re-derived at all; it was replaced with a fresh re-derivation against a live local fixture. Planning scope narrowed from a three-way remedy decision to a two-sentence documentation addition.

Sourcing scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh and running suite_selection_select directly over each planned Files-to-modify path produced verbatim, honest Tier Justification lines in one cheap call per phase -- including discovering that a specs/**/records/ path returns __FULL_SWEEP__, which selected the correct sub-case (prose diff read-through) instead of a fabricated gate subset. Also avoided siting the disposition note in specs/state.json, whose selector output is roughly seventy suites.

Two independent full bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh runs during Phase 3 each reported exactly one real, pre-existing, out-of-scope finding: agent-system/extensions/typescript/scripts/tests/test-typescript-verify.sh:40 fails lint-test-root-resolution.sh's guarded-REPO_ROOT-walk check. The file is clean in git (no uncommitted changes), last touched by an unrelated prior task (commit 35725799c, task 622), and lies outside both this task's file_scope and the declared concurrent sibling's file_scope. Treated as pre-existing drift, not a regression from this phase's edits, and not fixed here since it is out of scope.

Under heavy concurrent multi-agent CPU load (load average ~11 on 24 cores from many sibling verify-deploy.sh/lake/test invocations running simultaneously), specs/state.json schema validation (validate-state.sh --deep, gate10) exceeded its internal 60s timeout twice inside the full verify-deploy.sh/deploy-headless.sh fast-gate pass. Re-run standalone with a 180s budget, it completed in 66s with 0 failures (22 passed, 10 warnings). Confirmed as a load-induced timeout artifact, not a real validation failure, and unrelated to this phase's two-file documentation edit.

Phase 3's full-gate deferral directive worked exactly as designed: the two incidental full verify-deploy.sh runs (run before re-reading the dispatch's Batch Gate Deferral section carefully) surfaced only out-of-scope findings, corroborating that the scoped 8-suite run-all.sh --only discharge (test-context-reachability.sh, test-deploy-orphans.sh, test-index-entries-schema.sh, test-install-uninstall-extension.sh, test-manifest-scripts-sync.sh, test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, test-roadmap-command-registration.sh) is a faithful discharge for this phase's actual touched files -- all 8 suites passed green both in Phase 1 and again in Phase 3.
